subject.title: fix(security): add estimate-before-decode guard to base64 paths

question: Should OpenAI-compatible and Codex/OAuth image generation treat the existing configured image budget as a strict per-image decode limit, including failing a response when every returned image exceeds that limit?
rationale: The patch is mechanically coherent and proven, but it intentionally changes what an existing configured budget permits at the provider response boundary; tests cannot determine whether that compatibility/security tradeoff is the intended product contract.

options.title: Adopt strict per-image enforcement
options.body: Keep the new `maxBytes` propagation and accept that fully oversized responses fail through the existing missing-image error while mixed responses retain in-budget images.

options.title: Keep aggregate-only OpenAI-compatible behavior
options.body: Remove per-entry enforcement from the OAuth/OpenAI-compatible response path and retain the guard only where a per-item budget is already an established contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt strict per-image enforcement
recommendation.body: Keep the new `maxBytes` propagation and accept that fully oversized responses fail through the existing missing-image error while mixed responses retain in-budget images.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the adjacent CLI execution integration, and this decision spans that boundary plus the established generated-image runtime.
